blocks.h2: Why Arlington Heights Sewer Lines Need Maintenance

tiles.body: Most homes from the 1940s through the 1960s drain through clay. Roots return to the same joints every year.
A mature maple or oak near the sewer path will keep sending roots toward it.
One backup is often the first sign of a pattern.
Sewage on carpet and drywall costs far more than a yearly cleaning.

blocks.h2: How Often to Service Your Line
blocks.intro: A starting point. The camera fine-tunes it:
head: Your Situation
Suggested Schedule
rows: Rodding or jetting once a year, before spring storms
Jetting every 1 to 2 years, with a camera check
Clean line, no history of trouble
A camera check every few years
A camera check after a few years, then as needed

blocks.h2: Sewer Maintenance and Arlington Heights Storms
blocks.intro: On July 23, 2011, almost 7 inches of rain fell on Arlington Heights in just over three hours, and many homes had sewage back up into their basements.

items.h3: A Clear Line Handles Storms Better
items.body: You can't control how much rain falls. You can make sure roots and grease aren't already taking up half your line when it does.
Roots grow fastest in spring, and that's when the big storms start. Service before then gives the line its full capacity.

items.h3: Pair It With a Backflow Check
items.body: If your home has a backflow valve or an overhead sewer, a maintenance visit is a good time to check it too.

blocks.h2: What a Maintenance Visit Can (and Can't) Fix
blocks.intro: A maintenance visit is built around prevention, not repair. Here's where the line falls:
head: Included in a Maintenance Visit
Needs a Different Service
rows: A camera inspection to check your line's current condition
An active sewage backup. Likely fix: [Emergency Plumbing](/arlington-heights/emergency-plumbing)
Catching early root growth or wear before it becomes a bigger problem
A cracked or collapsed pipe. Likely fix: [Sewer Repair](/arlington-heights/sewer-repair)
A light interior clean as part of the visit
A heavy clog that needs full clearing. Likely fix: [Sewer Rodding](/arlington-heights/sewer-rodding) or [Hydro Jetting](/arlington-heights/hydro-jetting)
An honest assessment of what your line needs next
A line at the end of its lifespan. Likely fix: [Trenchless Sewer Repair](/arlington-heights/trenchless-sewer-repair)
blocks.note: If your line needs more than a checkup, we'll tell you exactly what and why. No surprise upsells.

blocks.intro: A maintenance plan is only worth it if it's based on your line.

steps.body: We look at the line before setting a schedule, so you don't pay for service you don't need.
Rodding for roots, jetting for grease and scale, depending on what we see.
You get the recommended interval and what to watch for between visits, priced upfront.

blocks.h2: Sewer Maintenance Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: Is sewer maintenance worth it if my line isn't clogged?
items.preview: If it's clay with trees nearby, yes. It's cheaper than a backup.
items.answer: If your line is clay and there are trees near it, yes. Roots grow back to the same joints every year. Clearing them on a schedule costs far less than cleaning up a finished basement.

items.q: What's the difference between maintenance and repair?
items.preview: Maintenance prevents problems. Repair fixes a damaged pipe.
items.answer: Maintenance is scheduled cleaning and inspection before anything goes wrong. Repair fixes an actual crack, break or collapse. A good maintenance visit tells you early if repair is coming.

items.preview: It helps. A clear line drains faster, but it can't stop an overloaded city sewer.
items.answer: It helps, because a clear line carries water out as fast as it can. It can't stop a city sewer that's overloaded and pushing back. For that, see [overhead sewer systems](/arlington-heights/overhead-sewer-systems).

items.q: Is sewer maintenance part of the No Drip Club?
items.preview: The No Drip Club includes regular maintenance visits. Ask us what fits your line.
items.answer: The [No Drip Club](/no-drip-club/) brings a plumber to your home for regular maintenance. Ask us how it applies to your sewer line when you call.

items.q: How much does sewer maintenance cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on the service and your line. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on whether your line needs rodding, jetting or just a camera check, and on access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
